facts.statement: The species name honors collector David Baldwin, while the genus name means "true hollow form" in Ancient Greek.
facts.quote: The species name honors David Baldwin, while the genus name was a reference to the status of the material as the original Coelophysis, derived from the Ancient Greek words eu ("true"), and coelo and physi meaning "hollow" and "nature".

facts.statement: Eucoelophysis lived during the Late Triassic (Norian) period in the Chinle Formation of New Mexico.
facts.quote: Eucoelophysis (meaning "true hollow form") is a genus of silesaurid dinosauriform from the Late Triassic (Norian) period Chinle Formation of New Mexico.

facts.statement: Research indicates Eucoelophysis is a close relative of Silesaurus and the sister group to Dinosauria.
facts.quote: a study by Nesbitt et al. found that it was actually a close relative of Silesaurus, which was independently supported by Ezcurra (2016), who found it to be the sister group to Dinosauria, and Silesaurus as the next most basal taxon.

facts.statement: Studies confirm Eucoelophysis is not a theropod or dinosaur but is related to Silesaurus and Pseudolagosuchus.
facts.quote: They found that Eucoelophysis was not a theropod or even a dinosaur, instead related to Silesaurus and Pseudolagosuchus (Lewisuchus).

facts.statement: Eucoelophysis is classified within the family Silesauridae.
It is debated whether Eucoelophysis represents a primitive ornithischian, though it is confirmed as a dinosauriform.
facts.quote: Dzik encontró que este es un dinosauriforme (el grupo de arcosaurios del cual evolucionaron los dinosaurios), pero no excluyó la posibilidad de que represente también un ornitisquio primitivo.

facts.statement: The time range for Eucoelophysis is estimated from 227.3 to 201.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Rhaetian (227.3 to 201.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Due to unclear vertebral features and pelvic differences, researchers retain only the hindlimb as definitive Eucoelophysis material.
facts.quote: The lack of clear features in the vertebrae, and differences between the pelvis of Eucoelophysis and Silesaurus, led Nesbitt and colleagues to only retain the hindlimb as Eucoelophysis, with the rest of the material as uncertain identity.

facts.statement: In 1887, Edward Drinker Cope initially classified specimens collected by David Baldwin as Coelurus bauri and Coelurus longicollis.
facts.quote: In 1887, Cope classified Baldwin's specimens as two new species of Coelurus: Coelurus bauri and Coelurus longicollis.

facts.statement: In 1889, Edward Drinker Cope created the new genus Coelophysis for three species from New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 1889, he again revisited their classification, creating the new genus Coelophysis for the three species, all from the same area of New Mexico.

facts.statement: In 1996, the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature designated a skeleton from Whitaker Quarry as the holotype of Coelophysis bauri.
facts.quote: In 1996, the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature designated a complete skeleton and skull from the Whitaker Quarry as the holotype of Coelophysis bauri.

facts.statement: In 2000, Andrew Heckert and colleagues identified fossils from the Snyder Quarry that may belong to Eucoelophysis.
facts.quote: In 2000, American paleontologists Andrew Heckert and colleagues identified Eucoelophysis-like fossils from the Snyder Quarry.

facts.statement: An articulated skeleton was moved to Eucoelophysis in 2009 but returned to Coelophysis in 2018 due to taxonomic re-evaluation.
facts.quote: An articulated skeleton (TMP 1986.63.33) from the Coelophysis quarry, previously considered a specimen of Coelophysis, was moved to Eucoelophysis by American paleontologist Larry Rinehart and colleagues in 2009, but it was returned to Coelophysis by American paleontologist Chris Griffin in 2018.

facts.statement: The bonebed locality where Eucoelophysis fossils were found included other reptiles such as Typothorax.
facts.quote: The bonebed locality included other reptiles such as Typothorax.
